title: The oil lamp
description: A little clay lamp with a cotton wick. Hear how it keeps the night away.

lines.text: Ah, you have found my lamp. We call it fitila.
It is shaped from the same river clay as the pot, small enough to sit in your palm.
We pour in palm oil and lay a wick of twisted cotton in its spout. Then we light the wick.
Before lanterns and electric light came, every home lit one of these at dusk. A whole street would glow with little flames.
ask: What did people use before electric light?

lines.text: My grandmother told her stories by the light of this very lamp, as I am telling you mine.
When the sun goes down, its little flame lets us find our mats, and tell stories late into the night.
Carry it upright and slowly, my child, or the oil will spill and drown the flame.
